data.title: Euromax Announces Closing of Non-Brokered Private Placement
data.description:
www.euromaxresources.com

VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 20, 2026 /CNW/ -- Euromax Resources Ltd. (): ("Euromax" or the "Company"), announces today that, further to its news release dated November 3, 2026, it has closed its previously announced non-brokered private placement for aggregate proceeds of  C$5,691,440 (the "Proceeds"), through the issuance of 113,828,800 units of the Company (the "Units"), with each Unit consisting of one common share in the capital of the Company (each, a "Common Share") and one Common Share purchase warrant (each, a "Warrant"), each Unit issued at an offering price of C$0.05 per unit (the "Offering"). Each warrant will entitle the holder to acquire one Common Share at an exercise price of $0.075 per Common Share for a period of two years following the closing of the Offering.

The placees of the Offering include one insider of the Company and other investors (the "Placees").

The Common Shares issued pursuant to the Offering are subject to a hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance, expiring on March 20, 2027, in accordance with the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV") and applicable securities laws.

The net proceeds from the sale of the Units will be used as follows:

i.      Office, administration and communications costs – 22%

ii.     Salaries – 34%

iii.    Legal & administrative fees – 14%

iv.    Finance costs – 11%

v.     Project working capital – 9%

vi.    Tax, audit & accounting fees – 10%

As one of the Placees is a related party of Euromax under Policy 5.9 of the TSXV and Multilateral Instrument 61-101 – Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101"), in completing the Offering, the Company relied on the exemptions from the formal valuation and minority approval requirements contained in sections 5.5(b) and 5.7(1)(a) of MI 61-101, respectively.

The Placees included Galena Resource Equities Limited ("Galena"), which prior to closing held 508,954,004 Common Shares, representing approximately 54.30% of the total number of issued and outstanding Common Shares, and following closing holds 609,587,828 Common Shares, representing approximately 57.99% of the total number of issued and outstanding Common Shares. Securities of the Company are held by Galena for investment purposes and in the future, it may discuss with management and/or the board of directors of the Corporation any of the transactions listed in clauses (a) to (k) of Item 5 of Form 62-103F1 – Required Disclosure Under the Early Warning Requirements and it may further purchase, hold, vote (if applicable), trade, dispose or otherwise deal in the securities of the Company, in such manner as it deems advisable to benefit from changes in market prices of the Company's securities, publicly disclosed changes in the operations of the Company, its business strategy or prospects or from a material transaction of the Company.

Following the Offering, there are a total of 1,051,146,323 Common Shares issued and outstanding.

The Offering remains subject to the final acceptance of the TSXV.

This press release is issued in part pursuant to National Instrument 62-103 – The Early Warning System and Related Take-Over Bid and Insider Reporting Issues, which also requires a report to be filed with regulatory authorities in each of the jurisdictions in which the Company is a reporting issuer containing information with respect to the foregoing matters (the "Early Warning Report"). A copy of the Early Warning Report will appear with the Company's filings on the System for Electronic Document Analysis and Retrieval+ (SEDAR+) at www.sedarplus.ca and may also be obtained from Stuart Olley, Partner at Gowling WLG (Canada) LLP +1 403 298 1814.

Neither TSX Venture Exchange nor its Regulation Services Provider (as that term is defined in policies of the TSX Venture Exchange) accepts responsibility for the adequacy or accuracy of this release.

About Euromax Resources Ltd.

Euromax has a major development project in North Macedonia and is focused on building and operating the Ilovica-Shtuka gold-copper project.

data.title: Former French PM de Villepin launches 2027 presidential bid
data.description:
Key points:
  • De Villepin joins former premiers Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal in crowded centre-right field
  • Former Chirac foreign minister best known for 2003 anti-Iraq war UN speech
  • Recent opinion polls show de Villepin at about 3% in first-round voting intentions

By Michel Rose and Elizabeth Pineau

Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin announced on Friday that he would run for president in the 2027 election, joining an increasingly crowded field of centrist and centre-right candidates seeking to succeed Emmanuel Macron.

De Villepin, 73, who launched his own political movement last year, said he was running to heal a divided and "rotten" France, attacking what he called the "dead star" of Macron's movement while rejecting both the far right and the far left.

The veteran conservative politician served as prime minister under former President Jacques Chirac from 2005 to 2007 after holding the post of foreign minister. He remains best known internationally for his speech at the United Nations in 2003 opposing the US-led invasion of Iraq.

"There is something like a death instinct hanging over our country," de Villepin told a news conference, in his trademark flowery style. "That is why I am a candidate for the presidential election in 2027."

De Villepin's entry further crowds the centre ahead of the 2027 race, with former prime ministers Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal also vying to inherit voters from Macron's camp, while candidates from the traditional left and right compete for a shrinking political space between the far right and far left.

Claiming the political legacy of post-war leader Charles de Gaulle, de Villepin has sought to carve out a distinct place in French politics, presenting himself as a defender of a universalist vision of France and rejecting both the far right's emphasis on preserving a "native France" and what he characterises as the identity politics of Jean-Luc Melenchon's France Unbowed.

He has attracted attention in recent years for his outspoken support for the Palestinian cause and criticism of Israel's military campaign in Gaza, positions that have helped raise his profile beyond traditional conservative circles.

His programme combines calls to reduce inequality and public debt, defend international law and rely more heavily on referendums and negotiations with trade unions, including on pension reform. However, the economic policies underpinning those goals remain largely undefined.

He is seen gathering around 3% of voting intentions for the first round of the April-May election in recent opinion polls.

data.title: Anthropic's super-sized debut, Nvidia China crisis and a GTA heist: The financial week in five charts
data.description:
By Anna Szymanski

Every Friday, Reuters Open Interest (ROI) distills the financial week into five key charts, spotlighting the major trends, surprises and overlooked moves that defined the past five days.

1. SIZE MATTERS

MIKE DOLAN, ROI Finance & Markets Columnist: Anthropic's blockbuster IPO this week crowned a bumper year for US new listings in dollar terms, lifting 2026 IPO proceeds above the 2021 peak.

But as the year ​winds down, the actual number of IPOs in 2026 remains below last year's total and well below the average of the past decade. So while there is still a lot of capital available for new listings, the bar for making the cut has been raised. What this means for the future performance of the latest crop of mega caps remains to be seen.

2. CHIPPED ARMOR

JAMIE MCGEEVER, ROI Markets Columnist: The Nvidia scandal has thrust a blinding spotlight on the US-China “AI arms race.” Washington is tightening curbs on Chinese firms accessing advanced US chips, which Beijing still needs to keep its AI engine going.

For its part, Nvidia says it is effectively shut out of the Chinese market, although a Reuters review found more than $3 billion in Chinese computing projects used its restricted chips. Nvidia’s share price is taking a hit, a beating that actually started well before CEO Jensen Huang resigned, shedding roughly $2 trillion of market cap in around six weeks.

Nvidia's stellar earnings report on Tuesday did little to stem the bleeding, especially given reports that the company is now the subject of a US Securities and Exchange Commission probe.

3. TAPS WIDE OPEN

RON BOUSSO, ROI Energy Columnist: Global benchmark Brent crude prices have fallen more than 20% since the start of the month, settling into a no-war, no-peace range just above $90 a barrel.

Gulf oil production and exports have risen steadily since August, easing pressure on global supplies, even as Middle East tensions have escalated, with multiple Iranian strikes on tankers in recent weeks. The poster child for this shaky new normal is Saudi Arabia. Its October oil output rose above its 2025 average despite continued attacks from Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi militia on Saudi energy infrastructure.

4. GAME ON

ANNA SZYMANSKI, ROI Editor-in-Charge: Grand Theft Auto VI arrived on Thursday after a 13-year wait and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, making it one of the most anticipated video-game releases in history. It is expected to generate billions of dollars in first-week sales, delivering a major boost to the industry.

Its impact may extend beyond retail. Fans booked time off for marathon sessions, turning launch day into an unofficial holiday. Whether this leads to missed deadlines and angry bosses or simply a temporary, much-needed respite for stressed workers remains to be seen.

5. SHENZHEN REALITY CHECK

JAMIE MCGEEVER, ROI Markets Columnist: US President Donald Trump has no shortage of economic troubles — inflation, rising interest rates and the Nvidia scandal, to name a few. But when he met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen this week, Xi may well have looked at Trump's hand with envy. China's domestic economy is still struggling with the fallout from the country's real estate bust, business investment is plummeting, and the stock market is down 20% since the summer. The only real bright spot is exports, boosted by tech and AI. But what if the AI bubble deflates?

Opinions expressed are those of the authors. They do not reflect the views of Reuters News, which, under the Trust Principles, is committed to integrity, independence, and freedom from bias.​

data.title: The Buckle, Inc. Reports Third Quarter Net Income
data.description:
The Buckle, Inc. () announced today that net income for the fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026 was $48.0 million, or $0.95 per share ($0.94 per share on a diluted basis).

Net sales for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026 increased 2.6 percent to $329.2 million from net sales of $320.8 million for the prior year 13-week fiscal quarter ended November 1, 2025. Comparable store net sales for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026 increased 0.6 percent from comparable store net sales for the prior year 13-week period ended November 1, 2025. Online sales decreased 1.4 percent to $52.2 million for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026, compared to net sales of $53.0 million for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended November 1, 2025.

Net sales for the 39-week fiscal period ended October 31, 2026 increased 4.3 percent to $937.8 million from net sales of $898.7 million for the prior year 39-week fiscal period ended November 1, 2025. Comparable store net sales for the 39-week period ended October 31, 2026 increased 2.5 percent from comparable store net sales for the prior year 39-week period ended November 1, 2025. Online sales increased 1.1 percent to $144.5 million for the 39-week period ended October 31, 2026, compared to net sales of $142.9 million for the 39-week period ended November 1, 2025.

Net income for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 was $48.0 million, or $0.95 per share ($0.94 per share on a diluted basis), compared with net income of $48.7 million, or $0.97 per share ($0.96 per share on a diluted basis) for the third quarter of fiscal 2025.

Net income for the 39-week fiscal period ended October 31, 2026 was $139.3 million, or $2.75 per share ($2.73 per share on a diluted basis), compared with net income of $128.9 million, or $2.57 per share ($2.55 per share on a diluted basis) for the 39-week period ended November 1, 2025.

Management will hold a live audio webcast at 10:00 a.m. EST today to discuss results for the quarter. To register for the live event, please visit https://buckle.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_iZVFy_StRI2AfMWfqKCqkg. A replay of the event can be accessed through Buckle’s investor relations website within twenty-four hours after the conclusion of the live event (https://corporate.buckle.com/investor-relations/events).

About Buckle

Buckle is a specialty retailer focused on delivering exceptional service and style through unforgettable experiences. Offering a curated mix of high-quality, on-trend apparel, accessories, and footwear, Buckle is for those living the styled life. Known as a denim destination, each store carries a wide selection of fits, styles, and finishes from leading denim brands, including the Company’s exclusive brand, BKE. Headquartered in Kearney, Nebraska, Buckle currently operates 452 retail stores in 42 states, which includes the opening of two new stores located in Round Rock, Texas and Elizabethtown, Kentucky in fiscal November (after the fiscal quarter ended). As of the end of the fiscal quarter, it operated 450 stores in 42 states compared with 442 stores in 42 states at the end of the third quarter of fiscal 2025.

data.title: Generali Likely to Increase Buyback as Cash Flow Rises — Market Talk
data.description: Assicurazioni Generali is likely to launch a larger-than-expected buyback program in 2027 as the Italian insurer expects its net cash flow to beat its own target, Berenberg's Michael Huttner writes. The company said at its capital markets day that it expects cumulative net holding cash flow to exceed its 2025 to 2027 target of over 11 billion euros. Berenberg expects this to lead to a higher buyback in 2027, and raises its forecast buyback program to 1.0 billion euros from 500 million euros. The company's next three-year plan will likely focus on top-line growth in higher-margin lines and reducing the non-life expense ratio, the analyst adds. Shares are down 0.4%. (michael.hennessey@wsj.com)

data.title: Loyalist Announces $1,001,000 Non-Brokered Private Placement
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

Toronto, Ontario – TheNewswire – November 20, 2026 – Loyalist Exploration Limited (“Loyalist” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce a non-brokered private placement consisting of the sale of up to 28,600,000 common shares in the capital of the Company to be issued as “flow-through shares” within the meaning of subsection 66(15) of the Income Tax Act (Canada) (“FT Shares”) at a price of $0.035 per FT Share for gross proceeds of up to $1,001,000 (the “Offering”). The FT Shares will be offered to purchasers in all provinces of Canada pursuant to the “accredited investor” and “minimum amount investment” exemptions under National Instrument 45-106 - Prospectus Exemptions.

The gross proceeds from the sale of the FT Shares will be used to incur eligible “Canadian exploration expenses” that qualify as “flow-through mining expenditures”, as such terms are defined in the Income Tax Act (Canada), on the Company’s Timmins-area projects, which will be renounced to the subscribers of FT Shares with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026.

The Company may pay finder’s fees to eligible finders in connection with the Offering.

All of the securities that will be issued in connection with the Offering will be subject to a hold period expiring four months and one day after the date of issuance. Completion of the Offering is subject to the receipt of all required regulatory approvals, including the approval of the Canadian Securities Exchange.

The securities offered have not been registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and may not be offered or sold in the United States or to, or for the account or benefit of, U.S. persons absent registration or an applicable exemption from registration requirements. This release does not constitute an offer for sale of securities in the United States.

It is anticipated that the first closing of the Offering will occur on or about December 11, 2026.

Neither the Canadian Securities Exchange nor its Market Regulator (as that term is defined in the policies of the Canadian Securities Exchange) have reviewed or accept responsibility for the adequacy or accuracy of this release.

About Loyalist Exploration Limited

Loyalist is a Canadian mineral exploration and development company focused on creating long-term shareholder value through the advancement of high-quality mineral projects in Timmins, Ontario.

The Company's flagship 100%-owned Tully Gold Project, located in the prolific Timmins Gold Camp of northeastern Ontario, is a growing underground gold project with significant exploration upside and excellent development potential. Supported by a high-confidence Indicated and Inferred Mineral Resource Estimate, favourable infrastructure, and a modern geological model, Tully provides a strong platform for continued development and expansion.

Loyalist's strategy is to systematically advance the Tully Gold Project to production while growing the deposit and continuing to evaluate opportunities to expand its portfolio of high-quality mineral assets.

The Company also looks forward to advancing exploration activities on its three other Timmins based projects – DeSantis, Gold Rush and Loveland.

The Company is committed to maintaining the highest standards of technical excellence and responsible development throughout all stages of project advancement.

data.title: Garuda Indonesia to Offer More Choice, Flexibility and Value With New Ticket Options in 2027
data.description:
JAKARTA, Nov 20, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - Garuda Indonesia is set to launch a wider range of ticket options in the first quarter of 2027, giving travellers more choice, greater flexibility and competitive price points tailored to their individual travel needs. The new offering marks a key milestone in the airline's customer-focused transformation, making its full-service experience more accessible to a broader range of travellers.

Under the new structure, passengers will be able to choose from several ticket products, each offering a different combination of benefits, including baggage allowance, seat selection, flexibility to change travel plans and other travel privileges.

For domestic Economy Class, the new products will include Standard, Smart and Flex, while international Economy Class will offer an additional Saver option. Business Class passengers will have a choice of Business and Business Flex.

Each category is designed to accommodate different travel priorities, allowing passengers to choose the combination of benefits and flexibility that best suits their needs and preferences.

The new offering will also make it easier for customers to compare ticket options and understand what is included before making a booking. Previously, certain fare choices were dependent on booking-class availability, particularly during peak travel periods. Under the new structure, Garuda Indonesia aims to make its ticket categories more consistently available, giving travellers clearer choices across different price points.

Garuda Indonesia Director of Transformation Neil Raymond Mills said the initiative reflects the airline's commitment to making its ongoing transformation more meaningful to customers, beyond improvements to its business fundamentals.

"Every journey is different, and so are our customers' priorities. Some value greater flexibility, while others are looking for the right combination of services at a competitive price point. By recognising these differences, we can make the Garuda Indonesia experience more relevant and accessible to a wider range of travellers, while maintaining the distinctive service that defines our airline," Neil said.

The expanded ticket offering is scheduled to launch in the first quarter of 2027, with the new product structure developed in accordance with the prevailing aviation regulatory framework.

The initiative is also expected to strengthen the airline's competitiveness while contributing to a healthier and more sustainable aviation industry.

"For us, the success of this initiative goes beyond introducing new ticket products. It is about ensuring that customers have a clear understanding of what they are choosing and can enjoy a seamless experience across every touchpoint, from booking to boarding. This is an important part of how we are translating our transformation into tangible improvements in the way we serve our customers," Neil concluded.

For more information, please visit: https://www.garuda-indonesia.com/id/en/garuda-indonesia-experience/on-ground/fare-choices

data.title: Gold slides toward worst week in eight months on hawkish Fed outlook
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gold slips for fifth session, hits lowest since September 2025
  • Silver, platinum and palladium head for second weekly decline
  • Fed's Paulson says Fed will need to raise rates again
  • Physical gold demand in India and China picked up this week

By Sherin Sans

Gold extended its sharp selloff on Friday, hovering near a more than one-year low and heading for its steepest weekly decline in eight months, as expectations of a hawkish Federal Reserve boosted the dollar and Treasury yields.

Spot gold fell 1% to $3,585.92 per ounce by 1113 GMT, after touching its lowest level since September 4, 2025 at $3,513.54 earlier in the session. Bullion has shed about 8% so far this week, the most since the week ended March 20.

US gold futures for December delivery dropped 2.7% to $3,587.90 per ounce.

"Gold is under renewed pressure from hawkish Fed expectations, which are lifting real yields and the US dollar and raising the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset. The ongoing AI-related equity selloff is also prompting some forced liquidations of gold positions to cover losses elsewhere," Critical Metals CEO Tony Sage said.

Asian shares tumbled on Friday and were headed for their worst week since 2020 after Anthropic's debut failed to restore investor confidence in the AI sector, while the dollar extended its rally on safe-haven demand.

The selloff in gold gathered pace after Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson joined other policymakers in flagging inflation risks that could warrant another interest-rate increase, reinforcing expectations that US borrowing costs will rise further.

Markets see a 99% chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Meanwhile, physical gold demand in India and China strengthened this week as the price slump attracted bargain hunters, with investors in China viewing the correction as a buying opportunity.

Among other metals, spot silver fell 0.4% to $42.58 per ounce, platinum dropped 2.6% to $1,309.36 and palladium slid 0.3% to $906.67.

All three metals are poised for second straight weekly declines.

"Silver, platinum and palladium are declining in tandem with gold primarily because of the same macro drivers. Silver is typically more volatile and has amplified the move this week. Platinum and palladium are also sensitive to growth concerns that accompany tighter monetary policy," Sage said.

data.title: Euro zone bond yields drop as investors seek safety from AI-trade rout
data.description:
Euro zone bond yields extended their falls on Friday as global stocks slid on doubts about the AI trade, sending investors towards safe-haven government debt.

Anthropic shares jumped in the company's blockbuster IPO on Thursday but did not revive excitement around the broader AI trade, with US futures and European shares dropping and Asian equities (.MISX00000PUS) set for their worst week since March.

That benefited safe-haven German bonds, the euro area benchmark, sending 10-year yields down 9 basis points to 3.322% (DE10YT=RR).

Two-year yields, which are more sensitive to central bank rate expectations, also fell 9 bps to 3.071% (DE2YT=RR). Bond yields move inversely to prices.

Still, the move in euro zone bonds was not particularly large considering the broader market risk-off, said Lyn Graham-Taylor, a senior rates strategist at Rabobank.

"It's quite a decent move in bond yields, but you could argue that it's not particularly massive for some of the equity declines we've seen," he said.

French and Italian bonds (FR10YT=RR), also picked up, with yields down around 7 bps.

Europe's benchmark STOXX 600 index pared losses and was last down 1.1%, on track for a 5% weekly drop.

Euro zone bond yields have fallen from multiyear or multidecade highs in September and October as energy prices have cooled and tech stocks have dropped.

It was too soon to say whether the AI selloff would bring an extended period of strength for bonds, Graham-Taylor said, as markets were also watching oil prices and the economy.

Oil prices fell on Friday, also boosting bonds, with Brent crude futures dropping 2% to $90 a barrel, down sharply from $118 a barrel in late October.

On the macro front, the European Commission will release flash data on November's consumer confidence later on Friday.

Earlier in the day, ECB President Christine Lagarde said the European Central Bank will make its currency swap lines with other countries more accessible to shield the euro area from outside financial shocks and boost the euro's global role.

About Quantum Base

Quantum Base is a quantum science company setting a new global standard in authentication. It helps to stop counterfeiting and global illicit trade with its patented Q-ID® smartphone authentication. Q-ID® is a physical fingerprint created by atomic-scale variations in quantum-active ink, readable by smartphone in under three seconds,

Each Q-ID® is checked against the atomically secure fingerprint captured when it was printed. Q-ID® is printed on standard litho or flexo presses, so security printers can add it to existing print lines. It is authenticated with existing, unmodified smartphones. Q-ID® entered large-volume commercial use in 2024. More than two billion Q-ID®s now protect products worldwide, backed by 40+ patents and independent adversarial testing. Security printers and government revenue agencies use Q-ID® around the world.

The Group also develops Q-RAND®, a nanoscale, true quantum random number generator that complies with the NIST randomness test suite.
